mainTopic: Can a young girl conceive and give birth while still a נערה? The גמרא challenges the setup of רבא's question about a נערה who was violated and died, then reframes it as a question about whether death makes her a בוגרת and ends the father's right to the קנס.
overview: The amud opens by testing רבא's question about a נערה who was violated and then died. The גמרא asks whether such a young girl could even conceive and give birth, citing a ברייתא about a קטנה who uses a מוך so she will not get pregnant. It suggests the whole pregnancy happened during נערות, but שמואל says נערות lasts only six months, too short for a birth. So רבא's question is reread: does a girl become a בוגרת in the grave, ending the father's right to the קנס? מר בר רב אשי asks it as 'does death make בגרות?', and the question ends in תיקו. Next, רבא asks אביי about a girl who became betrothed after the act. אביי rules the קנס still goes to the father, because אירוסין, unlike בגרות or נישואין, does not fully remove her from his authority. A new משנה then lists what a מפתה and an אונס pay and how they differ, including that the אונס must marry her unless she is forbidden to him. The גמרא begins asking what צער the אונס pays for, and רבי זירא challenges אבוה דשמואל's answer with a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Can a young girl even conceive?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the setup of רבא's question by quoting a ברייתא that says a קטנה who conceives may die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can such a young girl really get pregnant? רב ביבי taught that three women may use a מוך (a protective absorbent) during relations: a קטנה, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman. The קטנה, in case she conceives and dies. The pregnant woman, in case her fetus is crushed into a flat 'sandal' shape. The nursing woman, in case she has to wean her baby too early.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the basic picture behind רבא's question, which assumed a young girl became pregnant and gave birth. It brings a ברייתא suggesting that a young girl who conceives is in mortal danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's case needs a girl who gave birth before she became a בוגרת, so she would have had to conceive while still a קטנה. The ברייתא says a קטנה who conceives is at risk of dying from the pregnancy. That makes the case look unrealistic.

keyTerms.meaning: And can she really conceive? (a challenging question)
A soft absorbent material used to prevent pregnancy
A young girl who is not yet a נערה
A fetus crushed flat, shaped like a sandal-fish

phrases.english: And can she conceive?
phrases.notes: This is about the young girl in רבא's question just before this.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתָנֵי רַב בִּיבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Beivai teach before Rav Naḥman:
Three women engage in relations with a resorbent,
these are they: a minor, a pregnant woman, and a nursing woman.
A minor: lest she conceive and die;
a pregnant woman: lest her fetus become a sandal;
phrases.notes: A second pregnancy could crush the first fetus flat.

phrases.english: a nursing woman: lest she wean her son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind רבא's question, which was asked just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a young girl can conceive and give birth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא treats pregnancy in a קטנה as a deadly danger, so the scenario seems unrealistic.

steps.title: The ברייתא defines the age of a קטנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a קטנה here means ages 11 to 12. רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about whether she must use the מוך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who counts as a קטנה here? A girl from eleven years and a day until twelve years and a day. Younger or older than that, she has relations normally, says רבי מאיר. The חכמים say that all of them have relations normally, and Heaven will protect them, because the פסוק says 'ה׳ protects the simple.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא, which completes the proof behind the challenge. It defines the risky age and records a dispute about what to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before age 11 a girl cannot conceive at all, so there is no need for precaution. From 11 to 12 she can conceive, but it is dangerous for her. After 12 she is a נערה and the danger is gone. Either way, a girl younger than 12 who conceives is in danger, which supports the challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the age ranges. 'Less than this' means she is too young to conceive at all. 'More than this' means she is old enough that pregnancy is no longer dangerous.

phrases.english: And who is a minor?

phrases.aramaic: מִבַּת אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: From eleven years and one day old

phrases.aramaic: עַד שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: until twelve years and one day old.
Less than that or more than that,

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת כְּדַרְכָּהּ וְהוֹלֶכֶת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: she proceeds to have relations in her usual way; the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ
phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: both this one and that one
proceeds to have relations in her usual way,
and Heaven will have mercy,
because it is said: “The Lord preserves the simple”!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא used for the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That a girl under twelve cannot conceive safely.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רב ביבי, which defines a קטנה as age 11 to 12.

steps.title: Suggestion: she conceived and gave birth as a נערה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the whole pregnancy happened while she was a נערה, past the age of danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that she conceived when she was a נערה and gave birth while still a נערה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way to save רבא's case: the entire pregnancy happened while she was a נערה. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נערה is older than twelve, so the danger described in the ברייתא no longer applies. For רבא's case to work, she must also give birth before she becomes a בוגרת.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggested answer)
A girl just past twelve, before full adulthood

phrases.english: And if you say she conceived when she was a young woman,
and gave birth when she was a young woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pregnancy in a קטנה is dangerous, so the case is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole pregnancy took place during נערות.

steps.title: נערות lasts only six months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a full pregnancy cannot fit into נערות, which שמואל says lasts only six months.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can she give birth within six months? שמואל said that between נערות and בגרות there are only six months!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion. A pregnancy cannot be carried to birth within a six-month stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If נערות lasts exactly six months, a girl who conceives as a נערה will be a בוגרת before she gives birth. So the suggested timeline does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: The stage of being a נערה

phrases.english: But does she give birth in six months?
But didn't Shmuel say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין נַעֲרוּת לְבַגְרוּת אֶלָּא שִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים.
phrases.english: There is only six months between young womanhood and adulthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the whole pregnancy happened during נערות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נערות lasts six months, which is shorter than a pregnancy.

steps.title: Maybe six months is only the minimum
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל meant נערות lasts at least six months, and it could last longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say שמואל meant it is never less than six months, but it can be more...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to rescue the case by reading שמואל as giving only a minimum length. This sets up the next rejection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If נערות can last longer for some girls, a whole pregnancy might fit inside it. That would make רבא's case possible again.

phrases.english: And if you say: less is what there is not,
but more, there is,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the challenge from שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a statement as a minimum
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נערות is exactly six months long.
steps.terutzMaskana: נערות is at least six months long.

steps.title: The word אלא means exactly six months
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected because שמואל said 'only,' which means exactly six months.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said 'only'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the rereading by pointing to the word 'only' (אלא) in שמואל's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'there is only six months' sets an exact length, not a minimum. So the attempt to place the whole pregnancy inside נערות fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Only (here it limits the time to exactly this amount)

steps.whatToRemember: A girl cannot conceive and give birth within her six months of נערות, so רבא's question cannot have been about a living נערה giving birth.

phrases.english: But he said “only”!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer offered in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of שמואל as giving only a minimum.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the limiting word אלא.

steps.title: The real question: does she become a בוגרת in the grave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבא's question: after she dies, does she reach בגרות in the grave, so that the father's right to the קנס ends?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he was asking: Does she become a בוגרת in the grave, so the father's right ends? Or perhaps there is no becoming a בוגרת in the grave, and the father's right does not end?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier picture fell apart, the גמרא restates what רבא was really asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father's right to his daughter's קנס lasts only while she is a נערה. The question is whether a girl who died as a נערה is treated as 'growing up' after death, which would end the father's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he was asking

steps.whyThisMatters: It raises a real legal question: do stages of life keep counting after death for questions of who has rights?

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he was asking:
Is there adulthood in the grave, so the father's right lapses,
or perhaps there is no adulthood in the grave,
and the father's right does not lapse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the question that was rejected in steps 1 to 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא was asking about a נערה who gave birth and then died.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא was asking whether death leads to בגרות, which would end the father's right.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי's version: does death make בגרות?
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי asks the same question in a more general form: does death itself count as reaching בגרות?
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי asked it this way: Does death make her a בוגרת, or does it not?
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא, מר בר רב אשי, gives a different wording of the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of asking whether she grows up in the grave over time, he asks whether death itself puts her into the stage of בגרות. Either way, the practical issue is whether the father's rights end.

phrases.aramaic: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי בָּעֵי לַהּ הָכִי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi asked it this way:
Does death bring about adulthood,
or does it not bring about adulthood?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי בָּעֵי לַהּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second wording of the question in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether death counts as reaching בגרות.

steps.title: The question remains unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question is left open with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether death counts as בגרות, so the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether death counts as בגרות, which would end the father's right to the קנס, is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in steps 7 and 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is undecided whether death counts as בגרות and ends the father's right.

steps.title: רבא asks about a girl who became betrothed after the act
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks אביי: if a man forced a נערה and she later became betrothed, who gets the קנס?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked אביי: if he forced her and then she became betrothed, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a new question about timing. The girl was not betrothed when the act happened, but she became betrothed before payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קנס normally goes to the father. The question is whether her becoming betrothed afterward moves the payment away from the father, the way marriage or בגרות would.

phrases.english: Rava asked of Abaye:
If he had relations with her by force and she then became betrothed, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the קנס after the תיקו on death and בגרות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does אירוסין after the act take the קנס away from the father?

steps.title: אביי: the verse only cares about the time of the act
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the פסוק does not say 'a girl who is not betrothed' at the time of payment, so the father still gets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: is it written, 'he shall give to the father of the girl who is not betrothed'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the father still receives the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires that she was 'not betrothed' only when the act happened. The payment clause just says 'to the father of the נערה' and adds no condition. So betrothal afterward changes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: is it written? (meaning: it is not written)
and he shall give to the girl's father

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it written:
"And he shall give to the father of the girl
who is not betrothed"?
phrases.notes: There's no such פסוק. אביי is making up this wording to show that the תורה never added that condition to the payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קנס still goes to the father, because the פסוק sets no condition about her status at the time of payment.

steps.title: Challenge from the case of marriage
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: a ברייתא says that if she married, the קנס goes to her, even though the פסוק doesn't say 'not married' either.
steps.simpleTranslation: By your logic, the ברייתא says that if she married, the money is hers. Is it written 'to the father of the girl who is not married'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's reasoning using a ruling about marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we only follow the exact wording of the payment clause, then marriage after the act also should not matter. Yet the ברייתא rules that the money goes to her. So something besides the wording must count.

keyTerms.meaning: as was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And by your reasoning, that which was taught:
If he had relations with her and she then married, the fine goes to her:
Is it written "And he shall give to the father of the girl
who is not married"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that only the exact wording of the payment clause matters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same logic would give the קנס to the father after marriage, but the ברייתא says it goes to her.

steps.title: Marriage is like reaching adulthood
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers: marriage, like בגרות, removes her from the father's authority, so it follows the same rule as בגרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, since בגרות removes her from the father's authority and marriage does too, then just as with בגרות the money is hers, so with marriage it is hers.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why marriage is different from betrothal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With בגרות after the act, the money goes to her. Marriage, like בגרות, fully ends the father's authority, so the same rule applies to marriage. The marriage ruling comes from this comparison, not from the wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: How can you compare? There,
since adulthood removes her from the father's authority,
and marriage removes her from the father's authority,

phrases.aramaic: מָה בַּגְרוּת בָּא עָלֶיהָ וּבָגְרָה — לְעַצְמָהּ,
phrases.english: just as with adulthood, if he had relations with her and she grew up, the fine is hers,

phrases.aramaic: אַף נִישּׂוּאִין בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְנִשֵּׂאת — לְעַצְמָהּ.
phrases.english: so too with marriage, if he had relations with her and she married, it is hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Marriage and betrothal are treated the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Marriage fully ends the father's authority like בגרות, so it follows בגרות's rule.

steps.title: Betrothal does not fully end the father's authority
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves from a משנה that betrothal leaves the father with some authority: he and the groom together cancel her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: But betrothal, does it take her fully out of the father's authority? We learned: for a betrothed girl, her father and her husband cancel her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his answer by showing that betrothal is not like marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the father still shares in canceling her vows, betrothal does not fully end his authority. So betrothal cannot be compared to בגרות, and the קנס stays with the father.

keyTerms.meaning: betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.whatToRemember: After the act: if she reaches בגרות or marries, the קנס is hers. If she only becomes betrothed, it still goes to the father.

phrases.english: But betrothal,

phrases.aramaic: מִי קָא מַפְּקִי מֵרְשׁוּתָא דְּאָב לִגְמָרֵי?
phrases.english: does it take her completely out of the father's authority?
Didn't we learn: a betrothed girl,
her father and her husband cancel her vows.
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in נדרים 66b. Both of them together are needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵירוּסִין, מִי קָא מַפְּקִי מֵרְשׁוּתָא דְּאָב לִגְמָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's distinction with proof from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Betrothal does not fully remove the girl from the father's authority.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in נדרים: the father and the groom together cancel a betrothed girl's vows.

steps.title: New משנה: what the seducer and the rapist pay
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a מפתה pays three things, and an אונס pays those three plus צער.
steps.simpleTranslation: The seducer gives three things and the rapist four. The seducer gives shame, damage, and the fine. The rapist adds payment for pain.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a list of payments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both pay בושת, פגם, and קנס. Only the אונס pays צער, because a forced act causes physical pain.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The seducer gives three things,
and the rapist four.
The seducer gives payment for shame, damage, and the fine,

phrases.aramaic: מוֹסִיף עָלָיו אוֹנֵס שֶׁנּוֹתֵן אֶת הַצַּעַר.
phrases.english: the rapist adds to this, for he gives payment for the pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מפתה pays בושת, פגם, and קנס. אונס also pays צער.

steps.title: The differences between rapist and seducer
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three differences: צער, when payment is due, and whether he must marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference? The rapist pays for pain and the seducer doesn't. The rapist pays right away, and the seducer only if he sends her away. The rapist must marry her, and the seducer may send her away if he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues by listing the differences side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אונס pays immediately and must marry her. The מפתה pays only if he does not marry her, and he is free not to marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: drinks from his own pot (must marry her)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Drinks from his pot' is a picture, not a real drink. It means he is stuck with her as his wife.

phrases.english: What is the difference between a rapist and a seducer:
the rapist gives payment for pain,
and the seducer does not give payment for pain.
The rapist pays immediately,
and the seducer when he sends her away.
phrases.notes: He means the seducer pays only if he ends up not marrying her.

phrases.english: The rapist drinks from his pot,
and the seducer, if he wants to send her away, he may.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the differences.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the אונס pays צער, pays immediately, and must marry her.

steps.title: He must marry her, unless she is forbidden to him
steps.stepSummary: The אונס must marry her even if she has a physical defect, but not if she is forbidden to him, based on 'ולו תהיה לאשה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he drink from his pot? Even if she is lame, blind, or has boils. If she is found to have done something immoral, or she may not marry into ישראל, he may not keep her, as it says 'and to him she shall be a wife', a wife fit for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what 'drinks from his pot' means and gives its limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Physical defects do not free him from marrying her. But if the marriage would be forbidden, the obligation falls away, because the פסוק speaks of a wife who is fit for him.

keyTerms.meaning: to keep her as a wife

steps.whatToRemember: The אונס must marry her regardless of physical defects, but never if the marriage itself is forbidden.

phrases.english: How does he drink from his pot:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הִיא חִיגֶּרֶת, אֲפִילּוּ הִיא סוֹמָא,
phrases.english: even if she is lame, even if she is blind,
and even if she is afflicted with boils.
If an immoral act is found in her,
or she is not fit to marry into the Jewish people,
he is not permitted to keep her,
as it says: "And to him she shall be a wife,"
a wife who is fit for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the third difference listed in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אונס must marry her despite defects, but not if she is forbidden to him.

steps.title: What pain does the rapist pay for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking which צער the משנה means when it says an אונס pays for צער.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Pain for what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking a simple question: what exact pain is the אונס paying for? This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the אונס pays צער and the מפתה does not. That tells us there is a payment, but not what pain it covers. The גמרא wants to define the payment.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Pain: one of the payments an אונס owes

phrases.english: Gemara: Pain of what?
phrases.notes: He means the צער the משנה listed as an extra payment the אונס owes (step 15).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's explanation of the payment of צער mentioned in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific pain the payment of צער covers.

steps.title: The pain of being thrown on the ground
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל answers that the צער is the pain from the אונס slamming her onto the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל's father said: the pain from his slamming her onto the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: אבוה דשמואל answers the question. The pain is the physical hurt she felt when he threw her down on the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer ties the payment to a physical injury caused by the force used, the hard ground. It is not about the act itself. That narrow definition is exactly what the next step attacks.

keyTerms.meaning: The father of the אמורא שמואל
He slammed or threw her down

phrases.english: Shmuel's father said:
The pain of his slamming her onto the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The צער is the pain caused by being thrown onto the hard ground.

steps.title: What if he threw her onto silk?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא objects: by this logic, an אונס who threw her onto soft silk would not have to pay for צער at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: If so, if he threw her onto silk, would he also be exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges אבוה דשמואל's answer. If the pain comes only from the hard ground, then someone who threw her onto something soft would owe nothing for צער.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge shows the strange result of tying the payment to the ground. It suggests the צער must be about something more basic than the surface she landed on. Here רבי זירא only raises the problem. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: introduces a strange result of the view
Exempt, does not have to pay

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objects to it:
But if that is so,
if he slammed her onto silk,
would he also be exempt?
phrases.notes: He means exempt from the payment for צער, since there was no hard ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the definition given in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבוה דשמואל's claim that צער means the pain of being thrown onto the ground.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the payment depends on the hard ground, a soft surface like silk would cancel the payment, which seems wrong.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the pain is not about the ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא heads off the reply 'yes, he is exempt' by starting to quote a ברייתא from רבי שמעון about why an אונס does not pay צער.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that is indeed so, but it was taught: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: A rapist does not pay for pain, because...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא imagines someone answering, 'Yes, on silk he really would be exempt.' He rejects this by quoting a ברייתא. The quote stops mid-sentence here and continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's view gives a reason why an אונס does not pay צער, and that reason has nothing to do with the ground. This suggests the argument is about a different kind of pain. So the ברייתא is being used as a source to push against אבוה דשמואל's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: brings up a possible reply
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?
A man who forced himself on a girl

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking רבי שמעון just disagrees with the משנה. The key part is his reason, which comes right after 'מפני' on the next part of the daf.

phrases.english: And if you say, yes, that is so —
but wasn't it taught in a ברייתא,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
a rapist does not pay for the pain —
because...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רבי זירא's objection by blocking the reply 'yes, he is exempt' and bringing a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible reply that throwing her onto silk really does exempt him from צער.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's reasoning about צער does not depend on the ground, so the payment for צער must be about a different kind of pain.
